# SPE round 3 plan

Round 3 tests one change to config C. It splits the outage status check back out of the merged tool. Configs A and B do not change and act as controls. Round 2 had 4 misses in 5 rows, and the naive "same as last round" guess was closer on all 4. So this plan moves a number only where a config changed.

Defaults I chose because the prompt did not say:
- The core ticket set is the round 2 set, unchanged. I assume it has 20 tickets for the cost estimate. T17 is the highest ID cited.
- Priority accuracy is predicted for C only, because round 2 logged it for C only.

## 1. Specify

### Proposals from round 2

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt | F4 is open. It is the one config change this round, and it applies to C only. |
| P2 | Adopt, scored as a separate set | A and B are at 0.86. Mixing new tickets into the core set would break the "same as last round" baseline. The 10 hard tickets get their own rows. |
| P3 | Adopt as a default. You can veto it at approval. | F6 is open and D's cost rose from $0.003 to $0.004. Dropping D removes the cheap-model arm. F6 stays open and is marked parked with D. |
| P4 | Adopt | At n=3, B's 0.86 against a predicted 0.88 cannot be told apart from noise. n=5 applies to every config, so it does not count as a config change. |

### Requirements (to `spe/spec/spec.md`, round 3 table)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3-1 | Config C calls the outage status check as its own tool. All other C tools stay merged. | P1, r02 F4 | C's tool list has a separate `outage_status` tool. A code check confirms that C called it on every outage ticket. |
| R3-2 | A and B run exactly as in round 2. | Control, r02 log | The config hash matches round 2. |
| R3-3 | Add 10 hard tickets (mixed billing and outage), IDs H01 to H10, each with a labeled category and priority. | P2 | The answer key has 10 new rows, and the grader's oracle scores 1.00 on them. |
| R3-4 | A mixed ticket is labeled with the category of the team that must act first. Outage comes before billing. | Default. You can override it at approval. | The rule is written in `disagreements.md`, and every H label follows it. |
| R3-5 | Config D is not run. | P3, r02 F6 | The Workflow config list is `["A","B","C"]`. |
| R3-6 | Each cell runs 5 trials. A split cell can get up to 3 extra trials, for at most 8. | P4 | The trial count per cell is in the results. |
| R3-7 | The grader reads priority from `label.priority` only. | r02 F5 | A selftest case has "P1" in the draft reply and "P3" in the label. The grader must score it as P3. |
| R3-8 | Core-set and hard-set results are reported separately. | P2 | The prediction log has separate rows for each set. |

## 2. Predict

The baseline comes from `spe/predictions/r03-draft.yaml` and the regraded round 2 log.

| Metric | Set | A | B | C | Same as last round (A / B / C) | Why | Grader check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | core | 0.86 | 0.86 | 0.83 | 0.86 / 0.86 / 0.80 | A and B have no change. My assumption is that C's drop from 0.84 to 0.80 came from outage tickets that C could not confirm without the status check. Restoring the check should recover most of that drop. | `label.category` exactly matches the key |
| priority accuracy | core | n/a | n/a | 0.76 | n/a / n/a / 0.71 | F4 sent outage tickets to P3. The split tool restores the status lookup. I do not predict a full return to 0.78, because the other merged tools stay. | `label.priority` exactly matches the key (F5 fix) |
| category accuracy | hard | 0.70 | 0.70 | 0.68 | none (new set) | Each mixed ticket has two plausible categories, so I expect a drop of about 0.16 from the core set. C stays merged for billing, so I put it slightly lower. | `label.category` matches the H key under rule R3-4 |
| priority accuracy | hard | n/a | n/a | 0.65 | none (new set) | Mixed tickets often hide the outage part. That hurts priority more than category. | `label.priority` matches the H key |
| C outage-check call rate | core + hard outage tickets | n/a | n/a | 1.00 | 0.00 (r02, per F4) | Once the tool is separate and named, the agent should always call it. | Code check on `tool_calls` |

Cost is logged against the cap but is not predicted this round. D was the only config with a cost row in round 2.

## 3. Evaluate

### Gates before launch (halt on any failure)

1. Grader selftest. The oracle must score 1.00 on core and hard. Empty output and wrong labels must score 0. The R3-7 draft-versus-label case must pass.
2. Hard-set key check. All 10 H labels must follow R3-4, and the oracle must score 1.00 on them.
3. Regrade round 2 as a control. Using the round 2 transcripts, the grader must reproduce exactly 0.86 for A, 0.86 for B, and 0.80 for C on category, and 0.71 for C on priority.
4. Dry run on 3 cells with 1 trial each:
   - C on T17, the case where F4 was seen
   - A on H01
   - B on one core ticket

   For each, check the schema, check that C called `outage_status`, and check that cost is logged.

### Workflow (`spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js`)

- The script sets `const ROUND = 3` once. All prompt text and paths are built from that constant.
- Arguments: `configs: ["A","B","C"]`, `sets: ["core","hard"]`, `trialsPerCell: 5`, `maxTrialsPerCell: 8`, `budgetCapUSD: 30`.
- Trial schema: `{ticket_id, label: {category, priority}, draft_reply, tool_calls[]}`. Code checks run first. They cover schema validity, the category enum, priority in P1 to P4, and the outage call. No judge is needed this round.
- Trials get no read access to `grade.py`, the answer keys, or `spe/predictions/`. A transcript scan voids any trial that touched those paths.
- A cell is split when its 5 trials disagree at 3 to 2 or 2 to 3. A split cell gets up to 3 extra trials. A trial that would cross the cap is skipped, and the skip is logged.
- The run ends with a failure analysis and a completeness critic. The failure analysis assigns new F-numbers and checks whether F4 is closed.

### Cost estimate (not measured)

The base run is 30 tickets x 3 configs x 5 trials = 450 trials. At an assumed $0.03 to $0.04 per trial for A to C, that comes to about $14 to $18. Extra trials for split cells and the dry run add about 20%. The cap is $30. The run halts and reports if it reaches the cap.

## 4. Steps and commits after approval

1. Save your prompt verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`. Add the R3 table to `spe/spec/spec.md`. Log R3-4, P3, and the $30 cap as defaults in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Commit as `SPE r03 specify`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` with the header `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It also gets the author line ("Claude, approved by the user in plan mode"), the configs, every number above with its Why, and `same_as_last_round`. Leave `r03-draft.yaml` as it is. Commit as `SPE r03 predict: C splits outage check, D dropped, n=5, +10 hard tickets`.
3. Build the harness, the H01 to H10 answer key, and the selftest cases. Commit as `SPE r03 evaluate (harness)`.
4. Run the gates, then launch the Workflow. Close out when the completion notice arrives, not when the Workflow returns at launch.
5. Commit as `SPE r03 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
6. Learn step:
   - Add the round 3 rows to `spe/prediction-log.md` with Verdict and Closer, plus a "Which Why broke" section. Say plainly if the naive guess beat the predictions again.
   - Add new failure types to `spe/failures.md`. Mark F4 fixed or still open.
   - Add a "Proposed for round 4" table to the spec and write `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml`.
   - Update `spe/README.md`.
   - Commit as `SPE r03 learn` and tag `spe-r03`.

Nothing is pushed. The stop rule does not apply yet, because round 2 had 1 hit in 5 rows.

## Decisions you approve with this plan

- Drop config D (P3).
- Label mixed tickets with the category of the team that must act first, so outage comes before billing (R3-4).
- Set the budget cap at $30.
